body.text: What airline rules apply to carrying CPAP machines, insulin pens and needles in cabin?

Airlines and airport security permit CPAP machines, insulin pens, capped needles, and insulated cooling packs in cabin baggage when declared at screening. Lithium-ion batteries for medical devices must always travel in the cabin, and passengers requiring wheelchairs or in-flight power should register special assistance at least 48 hours before departure.

Under [TSA medical device screening rules](https://www.tsa.gov/travel/security-screening/whatcanibring/items/nebulizers-cpaps-bipaps-and-apaps), CPAP, BiPAP, and APAP units travel in carry-on bags, and lithium batteries must stay in the cabin. Under [TSA guidance for disabilities and medical conditions](https://www.tsa.gov/travel/tsa-cares/disabilities-and-medical-conditions), medically necessary liquids, syringes, insulin pumps, and cooling packs are exempt from standard 100 ml liquid limits when declared at screening.

For flights into Istanbul, [Turkish Airlines special assistance](https://www.turkishairlines.com/en-ca/any-questions/special-assistance-for-passengers/) offers complimentary wheelchair and boarding support. Confirm aircraft seat-power availability in advance or pack a compliant dry-cell CPAP battery for overnight flights.

body.text: Do you need a signed physician letter for prescription medications at Turkish customs?

Yes. Carry a signed English physician letter on clinic letterhead alongside copies of your prescriptions whenever entering Türkiye with prescription medications, injectables, or medical devices. Turkish customs permits reasonable personal-use quantities matched to your stay, while controlled drugs—such as opioids, sedatives, or stimulants—require stricter verification before travel.

Both [UK FCDO Turkey travel health advice](https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/turkey/health) and the [CDC Yellow Book international travel checklist](https://www.cdc.gov/yellow-book/hcp/health-care-abroad/what-to-do-when-sick-abroad.html) advise packing medicines in original labeled containers with a physician letter listing active conditions, generic drug names, doses, and allergies.

body.text: Where can you rent wheelchairs, walkers or recovery pillows in Istanbul?

Medical supply shops (medikal mağazalar) clustered near major hospital districts—such as Çapa, Cerrahpaşa, Şişli, and Kadıköy—rent manual wheelchairs, folding walkers, shower chairs, and wedge or neck recovery pillows by the week. Arranging delivery directly to your Istanbul hotel before arrival avoids searching unfamiliar streets after surgery.

Istanbul's hills and uneven pavements make a sturdy folding wheelchair or rollator walker valuable during recovery. Recovery wedge or U-shaped neck pillows are inexpensive to buy locally from medical suppliers and leave behind if luggage space is tight.

How do Turkish pharmacies handle emergency refills?

Turkish pharmacies (eczane, marked by a red 'E' sign) cannot fill foreign prescriptions directly, so emergency refills for prescription-only medicines require a local Turkish physician's e-prescription (reçete). Rotating 24-hour duty pharmacies (nöbetçi eczane) operate in every Istanbul district overnight and on Sundays for urgent needs.

As [UK FCDO Turkey health advice](https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/turkey/health) warns, foreign prescriptions are not directly valid at Turkish pharmacies. Bring your full supply plus a buffer in hand luggage. If a dose is lost, present your English physician letter with generic names to a licensed Turkish doctor, who can evaluate you and issue a local prescription if appropriate. faq.q: Does a CPAP machine count toward my carry-on allowance?
faq.a: Many airlines exempt a dedicated CPAP bag as an assistive device, but rules vary by carrier and fare. Confirm directly with your airline at least 48 hours before departure.

faq.q: Can I bring distilled water for my CPAP through airport security?
faq.a: Security rules generally allow medically necessary liquids when declared, though buying sealed distilled water (saf su) at an Istanbul pharmacy after landing is easier.

faq.q: Will Turkish pharmacies accept my UK, EU, or US insulin prescription?
faq.a: No. Foreign prescriptions cannot be filled directly in Türkiye. Bring enough supply for your stay or consult a licensed Turkish physician for an emergency local prescription.

faq.q: How do I find an open pharmacy in Istanbul overnight or on Sunday?
faq.a: Every closed eczane posts the nearest 24-hour duty pharmacy (nöbetçi eczane) on its illuminated window sign, and hotel reception can confirm by phone.

faq.q: Should insulin go in checked baggage to stay cold?
faq.a: Never check insulin. Cargo holds can freeze and ruin insulin, and delayed bags create immediate risk. Keep insulin in cabin baggage inside an insulated pouch.
